//regions: Run the functions in Seoul, beside the database.
Measured on the live deployment: `x-vercel-id: syd1::iad1::…` — requests
entered at the Sydney edge but executed in iad1 (Washington DC), while
Supabase sits in ap-northeast-2 (Seoul). Every query crossed the Pacific
at ~160ms per round trip, and a page issuing several of them could not
come in under a second however the SQL was written.
Co-locating with the database is the right trade even though the user is
in Australia: the browser pays ONE extra hop to reach Seoul, whereas the
function pays that hop N times, once per query. One 150ms hop plus 2ms
queries beats a 20ms hop plus 160ms queries the moment N exceeds one.
If the database ever moves, this must move with it. They are a pair.
